texts.preamble: Mahendra Trading Company Through ... vs The State Of Maharashtra And Others on 30 June, 2020 Equivalent citations: Aironline 2020 Bom 707 Author: Shrikant D. Kulkarni Bench: T. V. Nalawade, Shrikant D. Kulkarni (1) criwp370.2020.odt In The High Court Of Judicature At Bombay Bench At Aurangabad Criminal Writ Petition No. 370 Of 2020 Mahendra Trading Company, (Mahendra Radhesham Chauhan) Age : 30 yrs, Occu.: Business 4/202, Steel Plant, Main Road Maramangalathupatty Salem 636 030.. Petitioner Versus 1. State of Maharashtra (Through Neknur Police Station) 2. The Superintendent of Police Beed District 3. Food and Drug Department Beed District. ...
texts.facts: Both the proceedings are filed for relief of quashing of FIR No. 37/2020 registered with Neknoor Police Station, District Beed for the offences punishable under Sections 188, 272, 273, 34 of the Indian Penal Code and under Sections 26, 27(2)(e), 59 and 30(2)(a) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. 2. The first proceeding is filed by Mahendra Trading Company represented by Mahendra Radhesham Chauhan and the second proceeding is filed by Meghdoot Logistic represented by Proprietor Mr. Tilak Chand Jain. The FIR is given by Food Safety Officer. There was specific information to this office on 22/02/2020 that in container No. HR-84-7688, the prohibited substances like Gutkha were being carried. He contacted police and with the police he went to hotel where the container was found to be parked. When the contents of the container were checked, they found 48 bags of Pan masala, premium chewing (3) criwp370.2020.odt tobacco which was scented, cool lip flitter tobacco which was scented and Tobacco of Ganesh brand which was also scented and the value of these articles was around Rs.26,74,824/-. The description of the labels, packets showing the contents was recorded and the so called record like bilty which was with the driver Ravindra Kumar Rampal and other Mahendra Trading Company Through ... vs The State Of Maharashtra And Others on 30 June, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118609328/ 2 person in the company of driver, namely, Bittu Kunwar Pal was taken over. These articles are used as Gutkha, Pan masala and so the articles came to be seized alongwith the vehicle. In this State there is the prohibition to manufacture, posses, sale, transport such articles and such notification has been issued. The contents of these articles are harmful to human being and as after inquiry, it transpired to police and office Food Safety Officer that they were illegally transporting the aforesaid articles for sale in Maharashtra, action was taken and the crime was registered. 3. The description given on the packets show that the goods were manufactured by companies like Kay Pan Fragrance Pvt. Ltd. Ghaziabad, Tobacco works Pvt. Ltd. Bulamdshahr Road, Industrial Area, Ghaziabad, Tejram Dharma Paul Pvt. Ltd Sonepat, Haryana and Tejram Dharma Paul Pvt. Ltd. Nathupur Sonepat, Haryana. Samples are taken by Food Safety Ofcer of these articles. The description of the contents given on the packets itself shows that these articles are prohibited for manufacture, sale, transport etc in Maharashtra. (4) criwp370.2020.odt 4.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the driver was having necessary documents in support of the goods and as the vehicle was being taken only through Maharashtra, no ofence is committed. In support of this contention some tax invoices of Shiva Trading Company of Delhi are produced. It was submitted that the goods were to be taken to Salem, Tamilnadu and they were not to be ofoaded in Maharashtra. Photocopies of e-way bills are produced to show that they were valid from 19/02/2020 to 14/03/2020. At this stage it is not necessary for this court to ascertain the genuineness of the bills. One tax invoice of Printed laminated Foil in Rolls wherein 4760 Kgs is also filed on record by the petitioner. There is apparently no mention of this in the FIR. Such foil is used for preparing pouches may be of gutka. 5. When there is specific allegation of aforesaid nature, opportunity needs to be given to police to complete the investigation and to take steps against the concerned. The defence taken by the counsel of the petitioners that the goods were only in transit and they were to be taken to Tamilnadu was considered by this Court in similar matters like Criminal Application No. 250 of 2019 (Mahesh S/o Umashankar Gaud Vs. The State of Maharashtra) decided on 19/06/2019. The law developed on such cases was discussed by this Court. Not only the defence of aforesaid nature but other defences taken by the accused persons were considered by this Court and following observations were made by this Court. (5) criwp370.2020.odt "4) The learned counsel for the applicant, driver of the truck, submitted that tobacco was being transported from Uttar Pradesh to Bidar, Karnataka. He has produced tax invoices in respect of some of the materials which are shown to be seized. He submitted that under the notification in question of the Commissioner of Food and Drugs Administration, Maharashtra State, though there is ban on manufacture, storage, distribution, transportation or sale of tobacco which is either favoured, sainted or mixed with any of the said adhesives under the provisions of section 30(2)(1) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act") Mahendra Trading Company Through ... vs The State Of Maharashtra And Others on 30 June, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118609328/ 3 there could not have been prohibition on transportation. He also submitted that in view of provisions of Articles, 19, 301 and 304 of the Constitution of India, such prohibition order also could not have been issued. Admittedly, these articles are banned in Maharashtra under the aforesaid notification for the aforesaid purposes. The said notification is not challenged in the present proceeding and relief of only quashing of the F.I.R. is claimed. 5) The learned Additional Public Prosecutor has produced on record along with reply afdavit, the results of the examination of the samples showing that in all these samples nicotine was detected. He submitted that the point raised is already decided by this Court in the cases like Writ Petition No. 9865/2012 (M/s. Vishnu 7) The learned counsel for the applicant placed reliance on some observations made by the Apex Court in Civil Appeal Nos. 10373-10374 of 2010 (State of Gujarat V. Jayeshbhai Kanjibhai Kalathiya) decided on 1-3-2019. This was in respect of transportation of sand from Gujarat when there was ban on taking the sand outside of the State due to scarcity of sand. It was legally excavated sand and in that context the provision of Article 301 of the Constitution was considered by the Apex Court.
